beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: If Elon sold it all, a third could vanish. Here's how.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Play it out with an illustrative $100 billion of shares. Two things eat that pile, and the first isn't the tax.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: His money isn't cash in a vault. It's shares of his companies, so to give a single dollar, he has to sell first.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But who has $100 billion to spend? Few buyers, so each one pays a lower price than the last.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Say the price slides 30% as he sells. That's $30.00B gone, so the pile brings in only $70.00B.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Ouch. But that's still $70.00B to give away, right?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Thing two: he paid almost nothing for those shares, so nearly all of it is profit, taxed at up to 23.8%. A charity deduction won't cover it all.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: That's where the plan breaks. From $100 billion of shares, only $70.00B reaches a charity, and that's before tax.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So the very rich rarely sell to give. They hand the shares to a charity, which skips his capital-gains tax and lets the charity sell slowly.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: So he can't just sell it all. Then what happens if Elon sold it all?
